{{< include ../includes/setup-parameters.qmd >}}

On my planet, work does not come with a contract, because nobody has to be tricked into helping. On yours it does. So here is yours.

You already started. You completed onboarding the moment you watched the [orientation film](../educational-film.qmd) and answered the 20 Questions, which means the paperwork below is a formality. But your species does not believe a thing is real until it has been signed, so we have made you something to sign.

## The agreement

This agreement is between **Earth Optimization Services** (the Company, which is you and everyone else) and **you** (the Employee, who is also the Company).

**1. Position.** You are a Humanity Manager. The job is managing humanity. It is going poorly and could use you.

**2. Title.** Your title, separate from the job, is **President of Earth Optimization Services**. So is everyone's. You appointed yourself, because in a company everyone owns there is nobody else to do the appointing. You may rename yourself to anything: promote yourself to President of the Universe (there is no evidence the seat is occupied by anyone else, and the [proof](../proof/delusion-of-insignificance.qmd) is in the back), or demote yourself to Senior Vice President of Humanity Management, Regional Director of Not Dying, or Intern. The default is President because you run this, it costs us nothing, and it is the rare resume line that is both impressive and true.

**3. Place of work.** Earth. Remote work is permitted, in the sense that there is nowhere else to go.

**4. Reporting structure.** You report to everyone. Everyone reports to you. The org chart is a circle. We tried to draw it and stopped. As you are probably very busy, you have eight billion assistant Presidents to assist you with your extensive Earth optimization duties; each of them also has eight billion, one of whom is you.

**5. Duties.** Clear your items on the [To-Do List for Humanity](../strategy/humanity-todo-list.qmd). Hire two more Humanity Managers. Reduce the amount of suffering and dying on the premises, of which there is, at present, a great deal.

**6. Workplace conduct.**

- Wash your hands. Your coworkers are trying not to get sick, and the disease does not need the help.
- Be kind to your coworkers. There are about eight billion of them, and most are having a harder day than they are letting on.
- When you meet a coworker, the approved greeting is: *"I love you. How can I help you?"* Management is aware this is unusual. Management has reviewed the current greeting, which is suspicion, and prefers this one.
- Do not kill your coworkers. This was not on the original list. It is now.

**7. Mandatory disclosure.** You must acknowledge, in writing, that you are [retarded](../problem/i-am-retarded.qmd); that perfect information and perfect rationality are not available to you, or to anyone; and that you will spend every day reaching for them anyway. Everyone signs this clause. The ones who will not are the ones we worry about.

**8. Uniform.** The [official uniform](joke.qmd) is a shirt that reads "I am retarded." A permanent marker and any other shirt is an accepted substitute. Wearing it is how the other Managers find you.

**9. Compensation.** A planet with less suffering and fewer funerals on it. [Referral bonuses](../strategy/earth-optimization-prize.qmd) for every Manager you bring on. You are not paid in control, because being paid in control was the entire problem.

**10. Equity.** One (1) vote. The same vote held by the person who runs the Company. There is no larger share to give you and none to withhold. Your money, if you choose to invest, buys a return; it does not buy a bigger vote. Nobody's vote is bigger than anybody's. Your species finds this more suspicious than theft.

**11. Authority.** Your presidency does not let you sign anything, spend anything, borrow anything, or collect a dollar from anyone in the Company's name. You may not tell a bank, a reporter, a government, or a stranger with a checkbook that you speak for Earth Optimization Services, because you do not. What a majority of Presidents can do is decide what the Company does; carrying it out is the officers' job, and they are bound to do what the Presidents decide. You can win the vote. You cannot personally sign the check. This is on purpose: it is how eight billion people run one company without any one of them running off with it.

**12. Confidentiality.** None. You may, and should, tell anyone everything. The Company keeps no secrets, because secrets were how the last one robbed you.

**13. Non-compete.** You may not compete with the continued existence of your species. Everything else is allowed, including starting a company exactly like this one, which would mean you had already won.

**14. Probationary period.** Your entire life. You are reviewed continuously by the diseases, which are thorough reviewers and grade on a curve made of corpses.

**15. Termination.** This is an at-will position; you may stop whenever you like. The only resignation the Company cannot accept is death, and a large part of the job is getting the Company to stop having to accept it. You can also be removed for cause: claiming you speak for the Company, signing or soliciting money in its name, or using the title to harm other Managers. Removal revokes your vote and registration. It cannot stop you calling yourself President, which is true of every title and every person.

**16. Acceptance.** By remaining alive and doing any of the above, you accept this agreement, and [Love's Wager](../proof/loves-wager.qmd) along with it: one finite afternoon, staked against two infinities. Management has checked the math and likes its odds.

Signed, the Employee (President of Earth Optimization Services, or your chosen title): ___________________________

Signed, the same Employee, in their capacity as the Company: ___________________________

Date: _______________

Questions for Human Resources go to {{< var contact_email >}}. Human Resources is also you.

## The qualifying exam

Onboarding includes the 20 Questions. Here are the ones you cannot graduate without. It is open-book; the book is the answer. You may not fail as long as Question 1 is yes.

**1. Do you love everybody?**

Required answer: yes. This is the only question that can fail you. "Everybody" includes the people you find annoying, the people on the other team, and the people who are wrong on the internet. If your answer is no, watch the [orientation film](../educational-film.qmd) again until something happens.

**2. How many times over can your species end its own civilization with the weapons it already owns?**

{{< var nuclear_winter_overkill_factor_nounit >}}. Civilization only ends once. The remaining apocalypses were built to make a point to an audience that will not be there.

**3. How many times more do your governments spend on the military than on testing which medicines work?**

{{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio_nounit >}} times. For every dollar spent finding out whether a medicine works, that many go to the opposite of medicine.

**4. How many humans have their own governments killed since 1900, not counting the wars?**

{{< var democide_total_20th_century_nounit >}}. The category is called democide, which is murder with paperwork. The wars are separate and additional.

**5. After winning the Second World War, how much did your grandparents cut military spending?**

{{< var post_ww2_military_cut_pct >}}. They then stumbled into the largest economic boom in your history, mostly by running out of people to shoot. You are being asked for one percent.

**6. How many people died of disease during this exam?**

{{< var global_disease_deaths_per_minute_nounit >}} every minute, so check the clock and multiply. That is your starting workload, and it is why the job exists.

**Pass condition:** Question 1 is yes. Everything else, you now know, which was the actual point of the exam. Print your certificate.

## Your certificate

Print it. Frame it. Hand a blank one to the next person you hire.
